text:
alex: Heads-up — prepping new org+accounts for acme-ai. Need a concise preflight for cross-cloud GPU + networking quota requests and tags. Drafting checklist here, please annotate quickly.
maya: Nice. I'll start. Top-level buckets: org/account creation, billing link, IAM role templates, resource tagging, GPU quotas by region, VPC design + NAT/egress limits, service limits (ENIs, ephemeral ports), and cost guardrails.
tj: Agree. Also add preferred instance families (A100/RTX6000 etc), whether we allow spot/preemptible, and fallback smaller GPUs for capacity issues.
sophia: Quick note on regions — acme needs eu-west-1 + us-west-2 primary. Some clouds have limited A100 availability in eu-west. We should include fallback regions and model placement policy.
ranjit: I'll stub quota request text for both clouds. Make sure to include expected sustained throughput (tokens/s or vGPU-hours/month) — providers ask for numbers.
deploy-bot: new ticket created: INFRA-1489 "acme-ai org preflight" assigned to alex.
alex: OK starting checklist draft. I'll paste it — keep it short so it's copy-pastable into provider consoles.
maya: +1.
--- BEGIN CHECKLIST DRAFT ---
alex: [Org & Accounts]
- Create org (or copy naming template): acme-ai-prod / acme-ai-staging / acme-ai-dev
- Link billing account and verify payment method
- Apply standard tags: team:acme, project:acme-ai, env:prod|staging|dev, cost-center:AI-RD

maya: [IAM & Policies]
- Create roles: infra-admin, infra-operator, readonly, billing-auditor
- Service accounts: inference-runner, model-deployer, metric-collector (least privilege)
- Org policies: restrict region list, enforce customer KMS for secrets (if requested)

tj: [VPC & Networking]
- Allocate non-overlapping CIDR blocks for prod/staging/dev (example 10.10.0.0/16, 10.11.0.0/16)
- NAT/Egress design: central NAT per region or per-account? note: NAT gateway quotas and EIP limits can bite big traffic spikes
- Firewall rules: allow control plane ports, block wide-open SSH except jumpbox
- Peering / Transit: document route table entries for peering and expected route limits (AWS route table, GCP routes)
- Ephemeral port / conntrack: estimate ephemeral NAT ports for batch/streaming workloads

sophia: [GPU capacity & quotas]
- Per-region requested quotas: list GPU type + desired count + justification
  * AWS: p3.2xlarge (1 x V100) x 50, p4d.24xlarge (8 x A100) x 4 — OR request vGPU cores if using custom quotas
  * GCP: a2-highgpu-1g (A100) x 40, a2-megagpu-16g (A100 16x) x 2
- Include expected sustained usage: e.g., "Estimated monthly vGPU-hours: 30,000; avg concurrent jobs: 120; peak 200"
- Spot/preemptible policy: allow spot for batch training only, inference uses reserved/dedicated for latency SLOs

ranjit: [Service limits to pre-check]
- ENIs per instance, ELB target limits, cloud NAT ephemeral ports, persistent disk IOPS, project-level API quotas
- For GCP: check per-project regional GPU quota + acceleratedInstanceQuota and CPUs quota in same region
- For AWS: service-quotas for "Running On-Demand GPU instances", EIPs, NAT gateways, and security group rules per ENI

alex: [Sample quota request text — GCP]
- Copyable snippet for GCP console/SRE request: 
```
Project: projects/ACME-PROD
Quota: "GPUS (A100) in europe-west4"
Current: 4
Requested: 40
Justification: Serving inference for acme-ai product (latency-sensitive). Estimated vGPU-hours/month: 25,000. We need capacity for 24/7 inference with canary rollouts and regional failover. Contact: alex@redwood.ai
```

maya: [Sample quota request text — AWS Service Quotas]
- For AWS Service Quotas console / support case: 
```
Quota: Running On-Demand GPU instances (p4/p3 families) in us-west-2
Current: 8
Requested: 80
Justification: Production inference + staging and failover. We plan to use a mix of on-demand and reserved instances with autoscaling. Expected monthly vGPU-hours: 30k. Please escalate to quota team if needed. Contact: maya@redwood.ai
```

tj: [Networking request snippets]
- Request more Elastic IPs if using per-NAT EIP mapping: "Increase EIP limit from 5 to 50 for account acme-ai-prod due to high NAT throughput needs."
- If using GCP Cloud NAT, ask for higher NAT ephemeral port quota and project QPS limits where relevant.

ranjit: [Cost guardrails]
- Enable budget alerts per-project (thresholds: 50%, 75%, 90%)
- Tag enforcement and cost allocation export to BigQuery / Cost Explorer
- Recommend initial soft-spend cap for dev accounts

alex: [Operational prechecks before first deploy]
- Create one small test cluster with minimal GPUs to validate AMIs/container runtime and driver compat (NVIDIA drivers, CUDA, MIG if needed)
- Smoke test network egress, NAT throughput, and per-connection behaviour
- Validate IAM OIDC provider for workload identities if using k8s -> cloud APIs

sophia: Nice checklist. Suggest adding a quick matrix: preferred region mapping, fallback region, estimated time to increase quotas (some providers ~24-72h, others need sales approval).

maya: I'll add that to the ticket. Also pro-tip: open support cases with both quota request + short justification and a separate billing verification case to avoid delays.

alex: Action items:
- ranjit: copy these snippets into INFRA-1489 and create cloud-provider-specific cases (AWS/GCP).
- maya: drive tagging + IAM templates and post links to org repo.
- tj: prototype small test cluster in eu-west-1 and report back errors.
- sophia: confirm A100 availability in eu-west-1 and us-west-2 and propose fallback regions.

ranjit: On it. I'll aim to open AWS/GCP cases by EOD and paste links here.

deploy-bot: ticket INFRA-1489 updated: ranjit assigned, due 2026-04-03.

alex: Thanks team — this is solid. Keep replies short here with PR links / support case IDs only.
--- END CHECKLIST DRAFT ---
ranjit: opened AWS support case #56781234 (increase Running On-Demand GPU instances). Link: https://console.aws.amazon.com/support/cases/#56781234
sophia: quick note — in eu-west-1 A100 pods are limited, we should include a fallback to eu-central-1.
tj: test cluster spun up in eu-west-1 with 2x a2-highgpu-1g, driver install hiccup (nvidia driver mismatch) — filing tiny follow-up thread.
maya: tagging PR: https://git.redwood.ai/acme-infra/tags/3
alex: perfect. closing the loop here — will mark INFRA-1489 as in-progress once quota cases are confirmed.
